paper.citation: Wager, S. and Athey, S. (2018). Estimation and Inference of Heterogeneous Treatment Effects using Random Forests. Journal of the American Statistical Association 113(523), 1228-1242. DOI: 10.1080/01621459.2017.1319839.
paper.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
paper.source_locator: Appendix A 'Additional Simulations', arXiv:1510.04342v4 (10 Jul 2017) PDF p.30, equation (30) for tau(x) and Table 5 (p.30) for the (q, d) grid; the preceding paragraph states 'we generate data with a treatment effect function (30)'.

mechanism.name: Wager–Athey (2018) appendix design: effect spread over q signal coordinates

generation_equations.label: Outcome
generation_equations.expression: Y = m(X) + A tau(X) + eps, eps ~ Normal(0,1)

assumptions: SUTVA: one version of treatment, no interference
Randomised assignment: e(x) = 0.5, so unconfoundedness holds by design
Homoscedastic Gaussian noise with unit variance

properties.notes: Four active coordinates, each contributing a small additive logistic term; this is the 'dense signal' regime the source uses to argue forests have less advantage. Additive, so no interaction; nonlinear through each sigmoid.

estimand.name: tau(x0) = E[Y(1) - Y(0) | X = x0]
estimand.definition: Conditional average treatment effect when the signal is spread additively over q = 4 of the 6 coordinates; the estimand at a query point is the sum of four sigmoid contributions minus 2.

truth.expression: Conditional average treatment effect when the signal is spread additively over q = 4 of the 6 coordinates; the estimand at a query point is the sum of four sigmoid contributions minus 2.
truth.derivation: Closed form: a sum of four logistic sigmoids minus q/2, evaluated exactly; cross-checked by a second typing (loop form) and by the realised outcome column.

adaptations: The source varies q in {2,4,6} and d in {6,12}; this package fixes the (q, d) = (4, 6) cell so that the surface has an exact closed form with 4/q = 1.

The source's second experiment (p.20, immediately after Eq. 28) states 'we evaluated the ability of causal forests to adapt to heterogeneity in tau(x), while holding m(x) = 0 and e(x) = 0.5 fixed'; the same values are used here and stated explicitly. Eq. (27) on the same page uses a beta-density propensity with m(x) = 2 X1 - 1 for a different experiment and does not apply to this design.
The source writes (W - 0.5) tau(X); this package uses A tau(X) with A in {0,1}. The CATE is unchanged.
The source reports Table 5 over 20 replications; no replication experiment is run here.
